questions.question: In which state is Vijay Stambh situated?
questions.solution:
• Vijay Stambh: Rajasthan
  • Location: Chittorgarh Fort. Built by Rana Kumbha to commemorate his victory over the armies of Malwa and Gujarat.

questions.question: Who is credited with the establishment of Servants of India Society?
questions.solution:
• Servants of India Society: Gopal Krishna Gokhale
  • 1905: Established in Pune to train Indians of different ethnicities and religions in welfare work.

questions.question: In which year did the ‘Battle of Buxar’ take place?
questions.solution:
• Battle of Buxar: 1764 CE
  • Combatants: British vs. the combined forces of Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daula, and Shah Alam II.

questions.question: Who led the Congress in the second round table conference held in London?
questions.solution:
• Second RTC: Mahatma Gandhi
  • 1931: Gandhi attended this conference as the sole representative of the Indian National Congress.

questions.question: The mausoleum of the Taj Mahal was designed by _______________.
questions.solution:
• Taj Mahal Architect: Ustad Ahmad Lahori
  • Detail: He was the chief architect of both the Taj Mahal and the Red Fort in Delhi.

questions.question: What was the Swadeshi Movement called in the state of Andhra Pradesh?
questions.solution:
• Andhra Swadeshi: Vande Mataram Movement
  • History: In Andhra, the anti-partition agitation was deeply associated with the slogan of Vande Mataram.

questions.question: Who was famous for publishing a formula in 1827 that shows the mathematical relationship between current, resistance and voltage?
questions.solution:
• Ohm's Law: Georg Simon Ohm
  • Science: Defined the relationship between voltage ($V$), current ($I$), and resistance ($R$).

questions.question: When was the Defence of India Act enacted?
questions.solution:
• Defence of India Act: 1915
  • Context: An emergency criminal law enacted to curtail nationalist and revolutionary activities during WWI.

questions.question: Who was our first Prime Minister?
questions.solution:
• First PM: Jawaharlal Nehru
  • Term: Served from 1947 to 1964.

questions.question: Which flag of the Indian National Congress was adopted in 1931?
questions.option_1: A two colour flag with charkha made by cloth
questions.option_2: A blue colour flag made by cloth
questions.option_3: One colour flag with charkha symbol
questions.option_4: A tricolour flag made by Khadi with a Charkha symbol
questions.solution:
• 1931 Flag: A tricolour flag made by Khadi with a Charkha symbol
  • Fact: Adopted during the Karachi session of the INC.

questions.question: Who among the following made Ganesh Chaturthi popular as a public celebration in Maharashtra?
questions.solution:
• Ganesh Chaturthi: Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak
  • Purpose: To bridge the gap between Brahmins and non-Brahmins and provide a platform for nationalist mobilization.

questions.question: The Taj Mahal was built by:
questions.solution:
• Taj Mahal Builder: Shah Jahan
  • Motive: Built in memory of his beloved wife, Mumtaz Mahal.

questions.question: The Tata Iron and Steel Company Limited (TISCO) was started in the year ________ at Sakchi in Jharkhand state.
questions.solution:
• TISCO: 1907
  • Founder: Jamsetji Tata and established by Dorabji Tata.

questions.question: Indian Industrialists reacted against colonial policies that restricted business activities and formed an organisation in 1927. What was it called?
questions.option_2: Federation of the Indian Chamber of Commerce and Industries (FICCI)
questions.solution:
• FICCI: Federation of the Indian Chamber of Commerce and Industries (FICCI)
  • Context: Established on the advice of Mahatma Gandhi to protect Indian business interests.

questions.question: Who founded the All-India Forward Bloc Party?
questions.solution:
• Forward Bloc: Subhas Chandra Bose
  • 1939: Founded as a faction within the Congress after Bose resigned from the presidency.

questions.question: In the 1939 Tripuri Congress Presidential Election, Pattabhi Sitaramayya was defeated by:
questions.solution:
• Tripuri Crisis: Subhas Chandra Bose
  • Fact: Bose won the election despite Gandhi's open support for Pattabhi Sitaramayya.

questions.question: In the context of the Revolt of 1857, Mangal Pandey belonged to which Bengal native Infantry?
questions.solution:
• Mangal Pandey: 34
  • Revolt: He was a sepoy of the 34th Bengal Native Infantry at Barrackpore.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about Abhinav Bharat Society.
1) The society was a community of socialists believed in an armed revolution.
2) The society was founded by Jaya Prakash Narayan.
3) Mitra Mela, a revolutionary secret society was renamed Abhinav Bharat in 1904.
Select the correct statement(s) using the codes given below.
questions.solution:
• Abhinav Bharat Society: Both 1 and 3
  • Correction: It was founded by **V.D. Savarkar**, not JP Narayan.

questions.question: Which of the following was the first major and decisive victory for the East India Company on the soil of India?
questions.solution:
• First Decisive Victory: Battle of Plassey
  • 1757: Robert Clive defeated Siraj-ud-Daula, laying the foundation of British rule in India.

questions.question: Which of the following was the first Satyagraha Movement led by Mahatma Gandhi in British India?
questions.solution:
• First Satyagraha: Champaran Satyagraha
  • 1917: Fought for the rights of indigo farmers in Bihar.

questions.question: Under whom among the following British Governor-Generals was the new policy of ‘paramountcy’ initiated in British India by the East India Company?
questions.solution:
• Policy of Paramountcy: Lord Hastings
  • Definition: Stated that the authority of the Company was supreme or paramount over Indian states.

questions.question: Under which Act was the rule of British Crown established over India?
questions.solution:
• Rule of Crown: Government of India Act 1858
  • Change: Transferred power from the East India Company to the British Crown following the 1857 Revolt.

questions.question: On whose advice did Gandhiji spend a year travelling around British India to know the people of India?
questions.solution:
• Gandhi's Mentor: Gopal Krishna Gokhale
  • Fact: Gokhale advised Gandhi to keep his "ears open but mouth shut" during his first year back in India.

questions.question: Swami Dayanand Saraswati founded a reform organisation in 1875 that attempted to reform Hinduism. What was it called?
questions.solution:
• Arya Samaj: Arya Samaj
  • Motto: 'Krinvanto Vishvam Aryam' (Make this world noble).

questions.question: The Brihadeswara Temple at Tanjavur built by:
questions.solution:
• Brihadeswara Temple: Rajaraja I
  • Architecture: A masterpiece of Dravidian Chola architecture.
